title: Culturing human pluripotent stem cells from diverse culture histories
protocol: Test all cultures for mycoplasma upon receipt.
Maintain cultures in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 and 20% O2.
Change the culture medium daily.
Select low passage cell lines that have undergone whole genome or exome sequencing.
Monitor genomic integrity of cell lines by targeted sequencing or microarray routinely.
If the culture conditions for hESCs are known, prepare plates to match these conditions.
Coat one well of a 6-well plate with ice-cold Matrigel or Geltrex according to manufacturer instructions.
Rinse off excess briefly with PBS before plating cells in 2 ml warm KSR:mTeSR1 with 10 μM RI.
Coat a second well of a 6-well plate with 0.1% gelatin for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Rinse briefly with PBS and plate MEFs in MEF medium at a density of approximately 50,000 cells per square centimeter to coat the well to 100% confluence.
Allow MEFs to attach for at least 24 hours before plating hESCs.
Immediately before plating, rinse wells briefly with PBS and add 2 ml warm KSR medium with 10 μM RI.
Store cryovials of hESC lines in liquid nitrogen upon receipt until use.
Prepare and label plates ahead of time for thawing vials.
Pre-warm 21 ml of a 1:1 mix of KSR and mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI to 37°C.
Transfer the cryovial from storage into a floating rack in a 37°C water bath for approximately 1 minute or until partially thawed.
Quickly transfer cells to a 15 ml conical tube containing 10 ml of pre-warmed KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI.
Centrifuge the cells at 1000 RPM for 5 minutes.
Re-suspend the pellet in another 10 ml of pre-warmed KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI and centrifuge again.
Resuspend the resulting pellet in 1 ml warm KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 mM RI.
Plate 0.5 ml per well.
Change medium after 24 hours to remove RI.
Feed cells daily thereafter with either KSR medium on MEFs or KSR:mTeSR1 on Matrigel.
Under phase contrast microscopy, observe hESCs for prominent nucleoli and a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio.
Identify differentiation to non-pluripotent cell types by morphology changes, especially elongated or flattened cells.
Passage hESC lines once plates reach approximately 90% confluence using EDTA under feeder-free conditions.
Disperse hPSCs into small clumps of cells rather than single cells with EDTA for efficient colony dispersion.
Maintain high rates of cell survival while eliminating enzymatic treatment and reducing mechanical handling.
Rinse plates briefly with PBS.
Incubate plates with warm EDTA for approximately 5 minutes at 37°C, or until cells take on a rounded, bright morphology under phase contrast microscopy.
Monitor cells every minute if they do not spontaneously detach from the plate.
Aspirate EDTA gently once cells easily wash off the plate.
Wash hESCs off of the plate with 1 ml warm KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI using a P1000.
Re-plate entire cell suspension onto a Matrigel-coated 10 cm plate containing 10 ml KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI for expansion.
Disperse hESC colonies with EDTA once they reach approximately 400 microns in diameter.
Wash dispersed cells off the plate with 1 ml warm KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI using a P1000.
Re-plate cells onto a matrigel-coated well of a 6 well plate as described above in 2 ml of medium.
Eliminate differentiated cells from hESC cultures.
Mark regions of the plate containing differentiated cells under a microscope.
Aspirate marked areas during cell feeding without allowing cultures to dry out.
Use gentle EDTA passaging to enrich for pluripotent cells.
If widespread differentiation is present, identify colonies with undifferentiated morphology.
Pick identified colonies using a P200 pipette under sterile conditions.
Transfer picked colonies onto a fresh matrigel-coated plate containing 10 ml KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI.
Control residual differentiation and expand pluripotent cells as described above.
Label 10 sterile cryovials per cell line with the cell line name, date, passage number, and other relevant information.
Dissociate cells when they reach approximately 90% confluence using EDTA.
Aspirate EDTA and gently detach and re-suspend cells in 5 ml KSR:mTeSR1 + 10 μM RI.
Gently add an equal volume of ice-cold Freezing Medium to the cell suspension, pipetting up and down for 1 minute.
Distribute 1 ml of cell suspension into each cryovial.
Firmly cap the cryovials.
Transfer the cryovials to a freezing container and place at -80°C overnight.
Transfer the cryovials to liquid nitrogen (gas phase) for long-term storage.
